events.ai_basis: an informal reasoning agent, Rethlas, and a formal verification agent, Archon
a self-contained proof produced (with no human intervention) by Rethlas and subsequently verified by human experts

why: The monomial conjecture for all Noetherian local rings was settled before the snapshot: equal characteristic by Hochster–Huneke (case), mixed-characteristic dimension three by Heitmann (case), and all regular rings in mixed characteristic by André (2016, PMIHES 2018), with Bhatt's independent second proof (Invent. Math. 2018). Combined with Hochster's DSC⇔MC equivalence and André's own statement that his Théorème 0.7.1 directly implies the monomial conjecture, André's and Bhatt's events answer the whole statement; both were accepted by journals of record, so digested. Dutta's claim is withdrawn. Hochster's equivalence, Shimomoto, Tavanfar and Heitmann–Ma are reductions or adjacent results (none). The only post-snapshot items do not concern the MC: Rodríguez-Villalobos–Schwede addresses Briançon–Skoda (none), and the two Rethlas papers resolve different commutative-algebra problems (variant), so their AI credit, recorded for completeness, cannot attach to this problem. Ma's note is undated and gets null.
doubts: André's and Bhatt's main theorems are the direct summand conjecture; the step to the MC for arbitrary local rings rests on Hochster's 1983 equivalence, which the researcher read only through secondary sources, and on a summariser's rendering of André's 'implique directement' sentence. Bhatt's scope as whole relies on the same equivalence. Ju et al.'s AI role is coded from a thin quote that only names the agents; this has no effect, because the event is a variant.
